description: Capricorn zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (December 22 to January 19).
answer: In Western astrology, Capricorn is the tenth sign of the zodiac, a cardinal earth sign ruled by Saturn. It is traditionally associated with ambition, discipline, patience and dry, steady resilience. The Sun is in Capricorn from about December 22 to January 19. The exact dates shift by a day from year to year.

sections.heading: Capricorn personality traits
paragraphs: Capricorn's symbol is the sea-goat, a creature with the horns and front legs of a mountain goat and the tail of a fish. The mountain half explains the reputation: a sure-footed climber who keeps going up, one careful step at a time, towards a peak others might not attempt. The fish tail is less discussed but just as telling, hinting at an inner life and emotional depth that Capricorn rarely puts on display. People with this Sun sign are often described as serious, responsible and older than their years when young, then lighter and more playful as they age.

Capricorn is a cardinal earth sign ruled by Saturn. Earth signs deal in what is real and tangible: work, money, the body, structures that last. Cardinal signs begin seasons, and Capricorn opens winter in the northern hemisphere, so its initiative shows up as planning, organising and taking charge of the long haul. Saturn is the planet of time, limits, responsibility and maturity, a demanding teacher that rewards effort and patience. With all three combined, Capricorn is usually pictured as the builder of the zodiac, someone who takes duty seriously, respects tradition and prefers achievement that has been earned the slow way.

sections.heading: Capricorn strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Capricorn is the friend you call when something actually needs doing. It is reliable, organised and willing to carry responsibility that others avoid, and it keeps its word. Its patience is a quiet superpower: Capricorns can work towards a goal for years without needing constant applause, and they tend to learn from setbacks rather than be defeated by them. Practical wisdom comes easily, along with a realistic view of how institutions and people work. Beneath the composure there is often a wonderfully dry sense of humour, plus a deep loyalty to family and to the few people it lets close.

Capricorn's discipline can harden into rigidity. It may hold itself and others to standards that leave little room for rest, mistakes or play, and it can measure worth, including its own, mainly by achievement. Pessimism is a common shadow, an expectation that things will go wrong unless controlled. Emotional reserve can read as coldness, so people may not realise how much Capricorn cares. Workaholism, status-consciousness and difficulty asking for help are other familiar patterns. Many Capricorns carry responsibility so early that they forget they are allowed to set it down occasionally.

sections.heading: Capricorn in love and relationships
paragraphs: Capricorn usually approaches love the way it approaches anything important: carefully, seriously and with the long term in mind. It may take time to open up, preferring to see whether someone is dependable before investing emotionally. Once committed, it tends to be devoted, protective and practical in its care, showing love by turning up, solving problems and building a stable shared life. Capricorn often needs respect, reliability and a partner with their own ambitions. It values loyalty enormously and is rarely impressed by drama or grand gestures that are not backed by action.

The friction usually concerns warmth and time. A partner may feel that work always comes first, or that Capricorn's feelings are hidden behind competence. Capricorn, for its part, may feel unappreciated for all the quiet effort it puts in. What helps is naming the care that Capricorn shows practically, while also asking it gently for words and affection. Shared rituals, protected time together and a sense of building something side by side tend to suit this sign. Capricorn grows in love when it lets itself be looked after, rather than always being the one who copes.

sections.heading: Capricorn at work
paragraphs: Work is where Capricorn often feels most at home. It is strategic, persistent and comfortable with hierarchy, rules and responsibility, which makes it a natural fit for management, finance, law, government, engineering, architecture, project management and running its own business. As a leader Capricorn is usually calm, demanding and fair, setting clear expectations and leading by example. It is good at long-range planning and tends to earn authority gradually rather than grabbing it, which means its position, once gained, is often secure and widely respected by the people who report to it.

Pitfalls include overwork, perfectionism and a reluctance to delegate to anyone who might not meet its standards. Capricorn can also stick with a path long after it has stopped being satisfying, because quitting feels like failure. With money it is usually prudent, a natural saver who plans ahead, though anxiety about security can make it reluctant to enjoy what it has earned. Building rest into the schedule as seriously as meetings, reviewing whether goals still fit, and setting aside some money purely for pleasure can keep Capricorn's ambition healthy.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Capricorn decans
paragraphs: Capricorn's growth edge is learning that worth is not only earned. You are allowed to be valued for who you are, not just for what you produce. A useful practice is to schedule unstructured time, and to defend it as firmly as a work deadline. Notice when you are bracing for the worst and ask what a hopeful but realistic outcome would look like instead. Let people see more of your feelings, even in small ways, such as saying "I am proud of this" or "I could use a hand". Playfulness can be cultivated like any other skill. Keep the patience, integrity and long view that make Capricorn trustworthy, and let them include kindness towards yourself.

Capricorn divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly December 22 to December 31, belongs to Saturn; the second, about January 1 to January 9, to Venus; and the third, around January 10 to January 19, to Mercury. Each has its own page, and every Capricorn birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: Why do Capricorns seem so serious?
faq.answer: Capricorn is traditionally linked with Saturn, the planet of responsibility, so many Capricorns take on duties early and learn to keep their feelings private. The seriousness is often a sign of commitment rather than coldness, and their dry humour usually emerges once they feel comfortable.

faq.question: Who is Capricorn most compatible with?
faq.answer: Capricorn is often paired with the fellow earth signs Taurus and Virgo, who share its practical, loyal outlook. Water signs Scorpio and Pisces are described as offering emotional depth it may need. Cancer, its opposite sign, brings warmth and a strong home-and-family focus. Real compatibility depends on the whole chart.

faq.question: What are the dates for Capricorn?
faq.answer: About December 22 to January 19. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Capricorn decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Saturn, the second (10° to 19°) with Venus and the third (20° to 29°) with Mercury, following the rulers of the earth signs in zodiac order.
